title: Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia
text: Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia is an elevated total serum bilirubin concentration in a newborn infant. Clinicians monitor bilirubin trends by age in hours and assess risk factors for neurotoxicity. Phototherapy thresholds depend on gestational age and hemolytic risk.

title: Neonatal jaundice
text: Neonatal jaundice is the visible yellow discoloration of the skin and sclera caused by bilirubin deposition in a newborn. It is a clinical sign that can accompany hyperbilirubinemia; visible jaundice alone does not define a treatment threshold.

title: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome
text: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome is caused by surfactant deficiency in premature infants. It presents with tachypnea, grunting, retractions, and hypoxemia shortly after birth. Surfactant replacement and respiratory support are core management.

title: Surfactant replacement in RDS
text: Surfactant replacement therapy is used in neonatal respiratory distress syndrome when respiratory distress and oxygen requirement are consistent with surfactant deficiency. Early rescue treatment is considered in preterm infants with worsening respiratory support needs.

title: Transient tachypnea of the newborn
text: Transient tachypnea of the newborn is a self-limited respiratory disorder after birth caused by delayed clearance of fetal lung fluid. It causes tachypnea and mild hypoxemia that usually resolve within days without surfactant therapy.

title: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia
text: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia is a chronic lung disease of prematurity characterized by prolonged oxygen dependence and abnormal alveolar growth. It develops after neonatal respiratory distress syndrome in some preterm infants and requires long-term respiratory follow-up.

title: Neonatal pneumonia
text: Neonatal pneumonia is a lung infection in a newborn presenting with respiratory distress, fever or hypothermia, and abnormal chest imaging. Empiric antibiotics are selected according to age, setting, and local resistance patterns.

title: Antibiotic treatment of neonatal pneumonia
text: Empiric antibiotic therapy for neonatal pneumonia is started after cultures when bacterial infection is suspected. The regimen is adjusted to culture results and local epidemiology; viral causes do not respond to antibiotics.

title: Pulmonary atelectasis
text: Pulmonary atelectasis is collapse of lung segments with loss of aeration. In newborns it may follow airway obstruction or surfactant deficiency and is managed by positioning, airway clearance, and treatment of the underlying cause.

title: Retinopathy of prematurity
text: Retinopathy of prematurity is a vasoproliferative retinal disorder affecting preterm infants. Screening intervals depend on gestational age and birth weight, and severe disease may require laser or anti-VEGF therapy.

title: Apnea of prematurity
text: Apnea of prematurity is a developmental pause in breathing longer than 20 seconds or accompanied by bradycardia or desaturation. Caffeine citrate is used to reduce apnea episodes; dosing follows neonatal protocols.

title: Neonatal hypoglycemia
text: Neonatal hypoglycemia is a low blood glucose concentration in a newborn. Management includes early feeding or intravenous dextrose depending on severity and the infant's ability to feed.

title: Neonatal sepsis
text: Neonatal sepsis is a systemic infection in the first 28 days of life, classified as early-onset or late-onset. Blood cultures and empiric antibiotics are used when clinical signs suggest infection.

title: Group B Streptococcus infection
text: Streptococcus agalactiae, also called group B Streptococcus, is a bacterium that can colonize the maternal genital tract. Intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis reduces vertical transmission and early-onset neonatal disease.

title: Neonatal pneumothorax
text: Neonatal pneumothorax is air in the pleural space that can cause respiratory distress. Tension pneumothorax may require needle aspiration or chest tube placement.

title: Pleural effusion
text: Pleural effusion is fluid accumulation in the pleural space. In newborns it may be associated with infection, chylothorax, or other conditions and is evaluated by imaging and fluid analysis.

title: Hyaline membrane disease
text: Hyaline membrane disease is an older term for neonatal respiratory distress syndrome caused by surfactant deficiency. It is characterized by ground-glass opacities and air bronchograms on chest imaging.

title: Meconium aspiration syndrome
text: Meconium aspiration syndrome occurs when a newborn inhales meconium-stained amniotic fluid, causing airway obstruction and respiratory distress.

title: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
text: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn is failure of pulmonary vascular resistance to fall after birth, causing hypoxemia and right-to-left shunting.

title: Asphyxia neonatorum
text: Asphyxia neonatorum is impaired gas exchange around birth leading to hypoxemia and metabolic acidosis; management focuses on resuscitation and organ support.

title: Periventricular leukomalacia
text: Periventricular leukomalacia is white-matter injury in preterm infants associated with cerebral palsy.

title: Infant colic
text: Infant colic is excessive crying in an otherwise healthy infant; management is supportive.

title: Vitamin K deficiency bleeding
text: Vitamin K deficiency bleeding in newborns is prevented by routine vitamin K prophylaxis.
